behavior: Sequences orders on one in-memory thread with a Disruptor ring buffer and a replayable journal. SQL is a read model.
limits: Local journal recovery is distinct from later replicated consensus.

behavior: Packages the sequencer for Kubernetes, with snapshots, startup replay and readiness gates.
limits: The historical single-member tier is retained for study; current cluster operation follows YU12.

behavior: Checks credit, size, notional, restricted securities and price collars in memory before admission.
limits: These controls implement specific admission rules, not regulatory certification.

behavior: Publishes account, limit and security changes through transactional outboxes and versioned control feeds.
limits: Persistence, publication and engine acknowledgement are separate events.

behavior: Adds settlement states, journal-to-SQL reconciliation, regulatory export, transaction-cost analysis and scoped post-trade access.
limits: Post-trade JWT checks do not establish production authentication for the new Desk.

behavior: Closes a versioned EOD price snapshot, checks mark quality and publishes an overnight P&L chain.
limits: Stale or missing marks require an explicit decision; arrival freshness is not market observation time.

behavior: Stores historical ticks, queries symbol/time windows and supports replay. Later kdb+/q capture adds engine order and trade history.
limits: Historical datasets and licensed raw data are not distributed with the documentation.

behavior: Slices TWAP parent orders into scheduled children through ordinary risk-gated order ingress.
limits: Scheduling and child execution are separate; a submitted child need not fill.

behavior: Adds operational configuration for secrets, probes, resource limits and service delivery.
limits: Configuration support does not establish the health or security of a deployed installation.

behavior: Maps FIX 4.4 sessions, order entry, cancellation and status onto the sequenced trading path.
limits: Typed order fields and accepted units follow the current order-type contract.

behavior: Replicates encoded events using Aeron transport and SBE messages, with replay and epoch recovery.
limits: Replication alone does not provide the consensus model introduced by YU12.

behavior: Runs matching on a three-member Aeron Raft cluster, with leader election, snapshots and archive recovery.
limits: A successful local recovery case is not an unbounded HA guarantee. Preserve compatible core versions and retained history.

behavior: Matches by price and time, fills at resting prices, supports cancel and atomic replace, and snapshots the resting book.
limits: Current YU18 adds typed orders and cross-account self-match groups. Tracing drops observations rather than blocking trading.

behavior: Trades listed equity options through the same book and applies contract multipliers to exposure.
limits: Trading support is distinct from option valuation, Greeks or exercise processing.

behavior: Exports un-netted positions and counterparties at one consensus cut with reproducible bytes and receipt identity.
limits: An extract is an input to a risk engine, not a computed portfolio-risk result.

behavior: Adds CDM instrument representation and Treasury/corporate-bond terms and pricing inputs.
limits: Instrument-level failures do not justify substituting invented marks; per-instrument support differs.

behavior: Books OTC swaps and swaptions beside the matching book in the same consensus log. Adds reference-anchored price bands, a price-derived grid, sequenced CLOSED/PRE_OPEN/OPEN phases, historical tape replay and operator-scoped counters.
limits: Contracts export terms without valuation. Historical replay is not live data or a backtest; tick-rule sides are inferred. Active configuration may instead use an explicitly synthetic offline feed.

behavior: Builds immutable risk bundles, validates dated market inputs and external results, and displays job status and coverage. Components also extend order lifecycle and projection recovery.
limits: The accepted container path prices a closed synthetic Treasury-bill profile. Production risk remains unavailable.
